overview: Global markets face continued pressure as U.S. stocks slump amid escalating concerns over artificial intelligence, tariffs, and interest rates, while severe weather disrupts the East Coast and California's tides reach unprecedented levels. In commercial real estate, major market dynamics are highlighted by transactions such as Netflix acquiring a historic Los Angeles studio at a discount and ongoing shifts in national office vacancy rates. Locally in San Francisco, the state is poised to enforce drastic measures to boost housing production as the city struggles to meet permit goals, even as Google prepares to open its first store in Union Square. Meanwhile, Hawaii governance sees Governor Josh Green elevating deputy directors to lead state departments and demanding rapid oil spill notifications following significant environmental concerns surrounding the H-Power plant.

items.title: US stocks fall further as fears over AI intensify
items.summary: All three main US indexes were down in early trading, with the tech-dominated Nasdaq down almost 4% as AI fears intensified.

items.title: California’s Tides Are in ‘Uncharted Territory’ as Water Surges Higher
items.summary: A section of a pier collapsed and tide records were broken in San Diego, Santa Barbara, and Monterey as California's tides reached uncharted territory.

items.title: Stocks Slump Again as Investors Fret About A.I., Tariffs and Inflation
items.summary: Nvidia and other tech companies fell as investors weighed developments in global trade and the path of interest rates.

items.title: Flight to Quality Deepens Divide Among Major U.S. Office Markets
items.summary: The national office vacancy rate declined 140 basis points annually to 17.2 percent in October, though the recovery remains uneven across major U.S. cities.

items.title: Vornado Sells 49% Stake in 90 Park Avenue to Sixth Street, DivcoWest
items.summary: Vornado Realty Trust sold a 49 percent stake in its 41-year-old Class A office building at 90 Park Avenue to Sixth Street and DivcoWest.

items.title: Netflix Buys Historic Radford Studio Center in L.A. for $380M
items.summary: Netflix has acquired one of Los Angeles’ landmark film and television studios, the Radford Studio Center, for $380 million at a steep discount.

items.title: Law Firms Expand Office Footprints as Leasing Nears Annual Record
items.summary: U.S. law firms are on pace for a second straight record year of office leasing, with many continuing to expand their footprints.

items.title: In a city getting richer by the day, hunger is worse than at the height of the pandemic
items.summary: Federal cuts are squeezing working families in San Francisco, leaving hunger worse than at the height of the pandemic as tech money pours in.

items.title: State set to force S.F. to pass ‘drastic measures’ to boost housing production
items.summary: San Francisco is unlikely to meet a state-imposed deadline to issue 29,000 building permits by January 2027, prompting the state to force drastic measures.

items.title: Google to open first SF store as tech companies flock to Union Square
items.summary: Google is set to open its first San Francisco store as tech companies and younger tenants flock back to fill spaces in Union Square.

items.title: Green elevates 6 deputy directors to lead Hawaii departments
items.summary: Gov. Josh Green appointed six deputy directors to lead state departments as he assembles his second-term Cabinet.

items.title: H-Power Operator’s National Track Record: Sued, Cited And Fired
items.summary: Honolulu is joining jurisdictions aiming to sever ties with Reworld, the operator of the H-Power plant, following a 400,000-gallon leak.

items.title: Green Demands Rapid Notice Of Oil Spills After ‘Outrageous’ Delays
items.summary: Gov. Green demanded rapid notice of oil spills and expressed outrage over the delayed reporting of the H-power incident, calling it immoral.

items.title: H-Power Spill Calls For Transparency, Accountability And Prevention
items.summary: The H-Power spill has prompted calls for an independent investigation, accessible testing results, and enforceable prevention standards in Hawaii.

wiki.title: Infancy Gospel of Thomas
wiki.extract: The Infancy Gospel of Thomas is an apocryphal gospel about the childhood of Jesus. Together with the Gospel of James, it is one of the earliest and most influential sources detailing the activities and life of the young Jesus, although neither text is included in the New Testament canon. Its creation is generally dated to the second century. The oldest extant fragmentary writing is in Koine Greek and dates to the fourth or fifth century; Latin and Syriac attestations to a short form exist from the fifth or sixth century; and an 11th-century manuscript in Greek contains the earliest extant long form of the work. Variants flourished that expanded the infancy gospel by combining it with other stories in larger works and anthologies; the Gospel of Pseudo-Matthew is one example that proved popular in the Latin-speaking Western Church during the Middle Ages.
